acceptance: specy_road/worker_ops.py and specy_road/worker_adapters.py (each at the 400-line cap) are split by responsibility into smaller modules (for example delegate/launch, message/resume, slot and lease checks; and one module per harness adapter plus a shared base), each well under the cap, with every name other modules or tests import still importable from its old module path

Behaviour is unchanged: the full suite passes with no test edited except import lines, specy-road integrity reports no removed or weakened tests, and every docstring and comment moves with its code; the implementation summary maps each moved function to its new module
nodes.title: Split worker_ops and worker_adapters so parallel leaves stop colliding

acceptance: A roster entry can set harness_model (the id the harness CLI expects, for example claude-opus-5-5 for roster id claude-opus-5.5); the default adapters pass it to --model, falling back to the roster id; validate warns when a Claude Code entry's id contains a dot and no harness_model is set

When a worker exits non-zero before its first stream event, its error event summary includes the harness's last error line from the log (for example an HTTP 404 for an unknown model), not only a pointer to the log; tests cover the mapping, the fallback and the early-failure summary

Resume passes the same model flag as the launch on claude-code, codex and cursor (today all three default resume commands drop it, and Codex documents that a resume keeps only the conversation, not flags); tests pin the resume argv with and without harness_model.
nodes.title: A roster entry maps to the harness's own model id, and a failed start says why

acceptance: A roster entry can set available: false or paused_until: <date or datetime>, read from a local untracked roadmap/orchestration.local.yaml overlay (so availability changes need no push) as well as the shared roster; orchestrate plan skips unavailable entries for every role, and worker delegate and review delegate refuse them with the reason
Past review records by an unavailable entry still count at their commit; tests cover available: false, a paused_until in the past and future, and the overlay

When a worker is paused by a usage limit with a parsed reset time (M8.2), worker sync prints the roster entry and the reset time with the paused_until line to put in roadmap/orchestration.local.yaml; a test covers the printed line. (Depends on M8.2's paused-by-limit state; drop this sentence if M8.2 lands later.)
nodes.title: A roster entry can be marked unavailable without deleting it

acceptance: A Claude Code result line whose permission_denials list is non-empty records a permission_denied worker event naming each denied tool and its input, and flags the worker, even when subtype is success, is_error is false and the exit code is 0; a test replays such a line.

A usage limit is recognised from the turn's text, never its exit code: a Claude result or api_error text that claude_code_limits.classify_limit reads as a limit (including subtype success with exit 0, and exit 1 with no result line, where the last message is read from ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl), a system/api_retry line with error rate_limit, and a Codex turn.failed whose text says 'try again at <time>' each put the worker in paused-by-limit with the parsed reset time when there is one; a test replays one line per case.

Claude Code worker and reviewer launches either set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 in the harness environment, as harness-facts.yaml states, or the fixture row and the 'Backgrounded tests' paragraph of docs/orchestration-workers.md say that claude -p waits up to 10 minutes of idle for background work it started; a test checks the environment the wrapper passes.

The Codex memory overrides the launch passes are checked against the captured `codex features list` (memory v2 is on by default for fresh profiles since 0.165), and a key the capture does not list fails refresh-profiles --check instead of being passed and ignored.
nodes.title: Headless runs report usage limits and denied actions instead of looking like success

acceptance: harness-facts.yaml carries rows F1-F22 of the 2026-11-02 triage (recorded in a design note under docs/design-notes/), each labelled documented with the vendor URL or runtime with its capture; no row rests only on the unsourced OpenAI report; refresh-profiles --check passes after --render

WORKFLOW_WORDS also contains goal, loop, queue, persist, gist, fleet, teleport, remote and spawn; every identifier in the accepted captures that now matches has a relationship; a test shows a capture that adds persist failing the diff until it is classified

The Codex captures are refreshed from an installed codex-cli 0.166.0 or later (--version, --help, exec --help, features list), and docs/orchestration-workers.md cites the captured versions instead of 'codex-cli 0.165.0' and 'verified … on 2026-10-27'
nodes.title: The harness facts fixture takes the 2026-11-02 sourced findings and watches the new scope-escape feature names

acceptance: validate's Claude context line counts .claude/rules/*.md (recursive) beside the CLAUDE.md family and reports the auto-memory MEMORY.md (first 200 lines or 25 KB) as a machine-local note; a test with a rules file and a memory file covers both
Cursor's line notes nested AGENTS.md files below the root (applied when the agent edits a file there) and Copilot's counts .github/instructions/* files; a test covers each
A Claude instruction file over 4 MiB is reported as not loaded, never counted; a test covers it
nodes.title: The context meter counts Claude rules, auto memory, Cursor nested AGENTS.md and Copilot path instructions
